entry.title: DynamicsPLM: A Dynamics-Enriched Small Protein Language Model for Protein Variant Effect Prediction
entry.summary:
Predicting how mutations impact protein function and stability remains a key challenge in computational biology. Current state-of-the-art protein language models (PLMs) primarily scale parameter size on sequence corpora to capture evolutionary constraints but remain blind to the explicit physical dynamics of folded proteins. Conversely, models trained strictly on physical dynamics neglect critical evolutionary sequence statistics.

Source: bioRxiv Bioinformatics Preprints · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins

entry.title: Regional Signals Matter: Rethinking Global Pooling for mRNA Foundation Models
entry.summary:
RNA foundation models with diverse architectures have shown promise for learning representations of messenger RNA (mRNA) sequences. However, existing benchmarks commonly reduce token-level embeddings to transcript-level representations through global mean pooling before fitting a downstream probe. This aggregation does not explicitly preserve the identities of biologically distinct mRNA regions.

Source: bioRxiv Bioinformatics Preprints · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins

entry.title: deepTools4: Faster, Scalable, and Modernized Genomic Data Analysis. The deepTools suite is widely used for quality control, summarization, and visualization of high-throughput sequencing data.
entry.summary:
The deepTools suite is widely used for quality control, summarization, and visualization of high-throughput sequencing data. However, as genomic datasets grow in scale and depth, existing tools often become computational bottlenecks. We present deepTools4, a modernized framework designed for high performance, scalability, and enhanced usability, while maintaining seamless integration with the Galaxy platform.

Source: bioRxiv Bioinformatics Preprints · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins #combinatorics

entry.title: Machine learning dataset and benchmark for accurate T cell receptor–pHLA binding prediction
entry.summary:
Nature Computational Science, Published online: 26 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01073-y Hi-TPH is a large-scale hierarchical dataset that enables more accurate prediction of T cell receptor binding to antigens using protein language models and reveals how molecular components jointly contribute to prediction.

Source: Nature Computational Science · Tags: #bioinformatics #materials-science #genomics-proteins
